Binance Reserves Over $6.34B in Company Funds to Cover Hack Losses, Including $5B in Affected Tokens Binance said it has reserved over $6.34 billion in company funds to cover losses from the hack, including $5 billion already held in the affected tokens. It is purchasing the remaining tokens through market and OTC channels, a process that may take longer due to limited liquidity. The reserved funds are separate from approximately $3 billion in frozen assets. Binance will publicly verify user assets through its Proof of Reserves. — link

Coinbase Executives Plan Potential Sale of Up to 13.6M COIN Shares Worth $2.2B According to Coinbase's Q3 SEC filing, CEO Brian Armstrong, co-founder Fred Ehrsam, and President Emilie Choi adopted Rule 10b5-1 trading plans allowing potential sales of up to 13.6 million COIN shares, worth approximately $2.2 billion based on the October 29 closing price. Armstrong's plan covers up to 8.17 million shares between November 16, 2026, and October 2027, subject to predetermined price thresholds. These are planned transactions, not completed sales. — link

Tether Reports $1.5B in Q3 Operating Profit as Excess Reserves Nearly Double to $7.95B Tether released its Q3 2026 reserve attestation prepared by BDO, reporting $1.5 billion in net operating profit for the quarter, roughly flat quarter-over-quarter, and $4.5 billion for the first nine months, primarily driven by U.S. Treasury bills and reverse repos. As of September 30, USDT issuance stood at approximately $184 billion, with total reserve assets of $191.5 billion and liabilities of $183.5 billion. Excess reserves nearly doubled from $4.1 billion at the end of Q2 to $7.95 billion, while direct and indirect U.S. Treasury bill holdings totaled $132.4 billion. — link

Grayscale: Hyperliquid Generates $105M in September Revenue as Income Sources Diversify According to an October 30 report by Grayscale, Hyperliquid generated approximately $105 million in revenue in September 2026, roughly flat year-over-year. Core trading fees accounted for about 64% of revenue, down from over 90% in mid-2025, as income from third-party markets, distribution partners, and USDC reserve yield expanded. Non-core revenue doubled year-over-year to $38 million. Grayscale identified regulated U.S. market access as a potential growth driver, citing Kraken parent Payward’s plans to become the first CFTC-regulated HIP-3 deployer and ICE’s partnership with Trade[XYZ] to develop U.S.-regulated perpetual futures markets on Hyperliquid. — link
